untrustedSubjects.why: Their ids were in the task text, and their scratch filenames were on screen, before the pictures. The harness verdict is recorded as derived. Do not read a pass on any of these five as open-set recognition. For each, the entry in findingsForArt gives my honest view of whether the picture would have been named without the prompt.

findingsForArt.subject: player-on-a-toboggan
findingsForArt.finding: The only failing subject. Misleading feature: the POSE. The plank and the curled prow now match the Dufferin Terrace riders. The body does not. Those riders lean far back along one straight diagonal, knees bent up, feet planted on the deck at the curl. The player sits nearly upright with straight, raised legs, and its boots hang above the prow instead of tucking back on the deck, which the contract's own detail asks for. It is still recognisably someone on a toboggan (blind answer: `a child ... riding a wooden toboggan`). What fails is the match with the level's riders.

findingsForArt.subject: canal-lock
findingsForArt.finding: Now passes (the previous run failed it on the chamber floor). Ice is visible in the chamber, and the mitre, balance beams, pivot block, coping, snow and handrails are all there. Blind: `canal lock gates ... closed mitre gates between cut-stone lock walls`. The short dark handrails read as benches at first glance, and at w140 I was only 0.35 confident. I think I would have said `lock` unprompted from the V of timber gates between stone walls, but I cannot prove it.

findingsForArt.subject: granite-erratic
findingsForArt.finding: Passes on `a glacial erratic`, but I got the place wrong: I wrote `possibly the Okotoks Big Rock, Alberta`. Two things misled me. The dark flat shade plane on the big boulder reads as a split, sheared face, which is Big Rock's signature. And the pavement reads as city paving slabs, not wave-rounded granite. Nothing in the frame says sea.

findingsForArt.finding: Named `a cable-stayed bridge` at all three sizes, even with the top of the pylon painted over. The single leaning mast and the fan of stays make the read, and I think it would survive unprompted. I also guessed `possibly the Esplanade Riel, Winnipeg`.
